question: Tired of babysitting your coding agent?

hook_visual.intent: an event arriving, the rules choosing an agent, one round of work

points.claim: Agent Autoloop turns a command-line agent into a background loop on one machine, with no server and no dashboard.
points.spoken: It's Agent Autoloop: it turns a command-line agent into a background loop on one machine.
points.source_note: README: 'Agent Autoloop turns your command-line agents into a background loop.' and 'One machine, one install command. Runs on Windows, macOS, or Linux. No cloud server or inbound ports required.'

visual.intent: the terminal agent becoming a loop that runs on one machine

points.title: A background loop

points.claim: A schedule, a new GitHub issue or a production alert becomes an event, and the rules choose which agent takes it and in which folder.
points.spoken: A schedule, a new issue or an alert becomes an event, and your rules pick which agent handles it and where.
points.source_note: README 'How a piece of work flows': 'A 9:00 AM schedule, a new GitHub issue, or a production alert becomes a standard event sent to the kernel.' / 'Your rules decide which agent handles it and in which folder.'

visual.intent: three event sources feeding the rules that pick an agent

points.title: Events, then rules
points.sub: Your rules pick the agent and folder.

points.claim: The agent works one round and exits, so nothing is standing by and spending tokens while it waits for a decision.
points.spoken: The agent works one round and exits, so it isn't standing by and burning tokens while it waits.
points.source_note: README: 'The agent puts its result in its final message, and the process exits.' and from the demo output: 'No process is running for it now, and it is not spending tokens.'

visual.intent: the round finishing and the process leaving

points.title: One round, then exit

points.claim: When the decision is yours, a card reaches Slack, Discord or a desktop notification, and one command resumes the work.
points.spoken: When a decision is yours, a card reaches you in Slack, Discord or a desktop notification, and one command resumes it.
points.source_note: README: 'Cards reach you on Feishu, DingTalk, WeCom, Slack, Discord, or desktop notifications when you are needed.' and 'run agent-autoloop status to see it pick the work back up and finish.'

visual.intent: the card arriving, the answer, the round resuming

points.title: A card, not a dashboard
points.sub: One command picks the work back up.

catch: The catch: you need a recent Node, Git and an agent already signed in, and the CLI is still in Chinese.
catch_sub: Setup is one install command on Windows, macOS or Linux.

catch_visual.intent: the tools it needs and the untranslated output

cta: Would you let an agent work while you're away? Comment LOOP and I'll pin it.
